title: Treated-Population Log Density-Ratio Effects under Outcome Rarity
banked_reason: The delivered results establish a matched causal-nuisance phase on the public region epsilon_n(beta)^2 <= r_low, rather than the complete jointly indexed frontier requested in oeq:sharp-frontier.
gap_reasons: Stage 0.5 (typed) finding outside D0.R core-edit scope — kernel_substituted@oeq:sharp-frontier.
At beta=1/10, s=1 and fixed delta, the lower bound has order n^(-4/15), while the strongest delivered upper bound has order (log(n)/n)^(1/5), leaving a polynomial gap.
The uniform oracle-survival boundary remains unresolved between s/[3(s+1)] and s/(3s+2), including both endpoints and their possible logarithms.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery constructed elementary and bin-ratio estimators, a rarity-aware quadratic correction with honest intervals, and same-class nuisance lower bounds; a second solve established a matched public region and oracle-boundary bracket. The complete frontier still has a polynomial fixed-density gap and an unresolved oracle-survival strip, requiring new higher-order contraction analysis or a stronger lower construction. Two independent terminal assessments found no bounded repair at the field floor; banked as subfield with retry eligibility for a materially stronger construction, before any Lean formalization.
tldr: For the causal treated-population log-distribution effect, the paper proves density-aware absolute-risk and finite-sample honest connected-interval bounds on the unchanged H\"older benchmark with propensity and conditional densities unrestricted within the declared envelopes. The elementary bracket gives the exact consistency boundary \(n\delta^{1+1/s}\to\infty\). Normalized observed-law alternatives give the nuisance lower envelope, and an observable quadratic correction gives the upper rate \(r_{\mathrm q}=r_{\mathrm{low}}\vee\epsilon_n(\beta)^2\) for \(0<\beta<s\). These bounds match whenever \(\epsilon_n(\beta)^2\le r_{\mathrm{low}}\), including the rough-sequence frontier \(R_n\asymp L_n\asymp n^{-2/15}\) at \((\beta,s,\delta)=(1/10,1,n^{-1/5})\). Uniform oracle survival is proved for \(\beta>s/(3s+2)\) and excluded for \(\beta<s/[3(s+1)]\). The complete frontier, the exact oracle boundary within the intervening strip and both critical endpoints, and the sharp rates in remaining squared-pilot-dominant regimes remain open.
gap: Published pointwise density theory prices outcome rarity in directly observed samples. Existing causal density-ratio inference uses shape constraints or fitted finite-basis models. Neither supplies the uniformly sharp depleted-density frontier on \(\mathcal M(\beta,s,\delta)\).
fill: The project fixes the treated-population target and full public depletion range, then matches all-procedure observed-law converses with total estimators and finite-sample honest connected intervals. The field claim requires the complete frontier and a substantive causal-nuisance or oracle-survival characterization.
